name: PALAU

flag.title: Flag of Palau
flag.note: Blue sea, golden moon — peace & harvest

lead: Palau is a tiny island nation in the Pacific. Its 340 coral islands look like green pebbles on a turquoise sea. Its reefs hold so much life that people call them the Underwater Serengeti (a famous African wildlife park).

sections.wows: 7 things to make you go wow

geo: Palau lies in the western Pacific, roughly halfway between the Philippines and Papua New Guinea. A reef rings its 340 islands, with over 500 coral species and 1,300 fish.
The Rock Islands are hundreds of mushroom-shaped rock domes. They became a UNESCO World Heritage Site in 2012. More than 50 saltwater lakes hide among them.
animals: Jellyfish Lake on Eil Malk holds nearly a million golden jellyfish. They lost their sting after living alone for 12,000 years. You can snorkel right among them.
Warm bays shelter dugongs, gentle sea cows that graze on seagrass. Saltwater crocodiles, called ius, lurk in salty coastal swamps. They grow up to 4.5 metres long.
culture: The bai is a grand wooden meeting house. Painted panels on every beam tell a myth or a lesson. The last original-style bai, in Airai village, is at least 180 years old.
Palau is matrilineal (mother-led). Land and clan titles pass down through mothers. The full moon is the best time for fishing and feasting.
history: People settled Palau at least 3,000 years ago. Spain claimed the islands in 1885. It sold them to Germany in 1899. Japan took them in 1914. The 1944 Battle of Peleliu lasted 74 brutal days.
After World War II, the USA ran Palau for the UN. Palau became independent on 1 October 1994. It signed a Compact of Free Association, a deal with the USA.
wows: Ngerulmud is the world's least-populous national capital.
Palau made Earth's first national shark sanctuary in 2009, covering 600,000 km².
Palau was first to ban reef-harming sunscreen chemicals, from 2020.
Visitors sign the Palau Pledge, a promise stamped into their passport.
Jellyfish Lake's golden jellyfish are found nowhere else on Earth.
Palau has closed 80% of its ocean waters to fishing.
The Rock Islands are the Pacific Islands' only UNESCO site for nature and culture.

myths.fact: Sharks rarely bite people. Most prefer fish. Divers in Palau swim near reef sharks at Blue Corner.
Coral is made of tiny animals called polyps, cousins of jellyfish.
